p: Numbers first. Lalla Nail Branch 1 holds {rR}★ from {rV} Google reviews, one of the largest samples of any nail salon in the city, and it closes at 21:00, an hour after Reborn. If your plan is a gel colour after dinner, or you simply trust the bigger sample, it is a sound choice.
It also sits on An Thượng 29, inside the grid of small streets where many visitors to My An stay, so for a lot of readers it is the nearer door.

Reborn is built for the longer visit. Its menu puts gel, BIAB and GelX next to four spa pedicure rituals and eight Vietnamese herbal head spa rituals, from a 25-minute wash at 120K to a 105-minute ritual at 850K. Two technicians can work at once, so nails and a head spa share one sitting instead of two appointments.

The other difference is the conversation. The owner, Fiona, runs the floor, and a Google reviewer wrote that she “speaks excellent English”. The menu on the salon's iPad comes in 20 languages, Korean, Chinese, Japanese and Russian included, with each price on screen before anything starts.

sections.h: What English-speaking means in a Da Nang salon
p: In the tourist quarters, most technicians manage the basics in English: colour, shape, length, price. Anything that needs explaining is harder, for example why a BIAB overlay suits short nails, what removal will cost next time, or whether a chrome design will survive a week of sea water. For that conversation you need someone at the desk who can hold it.
Screenshots and a translation app cover the rest. Bring a photo of the shape and colour you want; every salon on this list works from references.

For each of the {total} salons in this guide, we read the Google reviews returned by the Places API (up to five per salon, snapshot of {date}) and kept the ones where a reviewer mentions English. This shows that a reviewer found it worth mentioning. It is not a language test, and a salon absent from this list may well speak English too. The editors place our pick first, for the reasons above.

sections.h: Three questions to send on WhatsApp first
p: Send the photo, ask for the price including removal, and ask how long it takes. A salon that answers all three clearly in English is one you can talk to at the chair.

sections.h: A hair wash and a head spa are not the same booking
p: Plenty of Da Nang nail salons add a shampoo: a wash, a short scalp massage, a blow-dry, often from about 100K. A head spa is a longer ritual built around the scalp, with a herbal soak, steam, masks and neck and shoulder work, sometimes facial care, from about 45 minutes to well over an hour.
If you only want clean hair after the beach, any place on this list will do. If the head spa is the treat of the trip, look for a menu with several rituals and the minutes written next to each.

Ask for two technicians. At {N} a manicure and a head, neck or foot massage can run in the same sitting, according to the salon's menu. Message on WhatsApp to book that, especially for a weekend afternoon.

We kept every venue in our Google Places snapshot ({date}) whose listing name mentions nails together with a shampoo, hair wash or head spa, in English, Vietnamese or Korean. The name is the venue's own description of what it does; we have not checked each menu. Our pick is placed first by the editors.

pages.title: How to Spot Fake Reviews of Nail Salons in Da Nang
pages.desc: How to tell genuine Google reviews from padded ones before you book a nail salon in Da Nang: what to read first, the warning signs, and what real reviews look like.
pages.h1: How to spot fake reviews of nail salons in Da Nang
pages.lede: Almost every salon in the tourist quarters shows 4.8 to 5.0 stars. The stars cannot tell you much; the reviews behind them can, if you read them in the right order.
pages.q: How can you tell if a Da Nang nail salon's Google reviews are fake?
pages.answer: Sort the reviews by Newest and read the past three months before you check the average. The signs to watch for are a burst of reviews over a few days following a quiet spell, several five-star reviews posted minutes apart, a high share of stars without text, reviewers with only one review and no photo, near-identical wording, and offers of a discount in return for a review, which Google's rules do not allow. A single sign proves nothing by itself. Several together deserve a second look.

sections.h: Read them in date order first
p: Open the salon on Google Maps, tap Reviews and switch the sort to Newest. Then scroll back three months. In My An, a busy salon gets a review every day or two, spread over the week and written in several languages, with the occasional four-star among the fives. Faking that rhythm for long is hard.
Next, read the lowest ratings. The way the owner replies to a complaint says more about the visit you will have than fifty more five-star reviews.

sections.h: A burst after a quiet spell
p: Look out for a sudden run of reviews (say fifteen in two days) after weeks with almost none, or for a steady flow that stops dead. Real customers do not coordinate. When five-star reviews come in clusters posted within minutes of one another, that is one of the clearer signs of a campaign.

Leaving a star rating without text is allowed, and many genuine customers do it. A page on which a large share of the recent five-star reviews carry no text at all is another matter: such a review costs nothing to post and says nothing you can check.

Tap on a reviewer's name. One review, no photo and a generic name make an account weak evidence, particularly when several such accounts turn up in the same week. The opposite is a traveller who reviews hotels and restaurants during the same trip.
Read five recent reviews one after another. They may have been written from a template if they share phrasing, put the compliments in the same order, or praise the same technician in the same words.

Certain salons offer a discount, a free add-on or a gift in exchange for a Google review. That is not allowed under Google's review policy. A rating built on rewards is inflated even when every reviewer was a real customer, and the same applies to asking only happy customers for a review: an honest salon asks everyone.

Google takes down reviews that it judges to break its rules. If a salon's review count drops by dozens in a matter of days, many reviews have been removed. Which ones, you will not see. Still, it is a reason to read the recent reviews that remain with care.

Specifics. The technician's name, the treatment, what it cost, how long it took, a photo of the nails a few days afterwards, a complaint about the wait with an answer from the owner. Genuine review pages are slightly uneven, which is reassuring.

sections.h: How this guide uses review data
p: Each ranking on this site prints every salon's Google rating and review count alongside the date of the snapshot they are taken from, while our comparison pages show how a salon's review count changed from one snapshot to the next. The methodology page sets out how a rating is weighed against the number of reviews behind it. For anything no review can tell you, use the 90-second check at the door.

pages.verdict: A long, steady history of specific reviews deserves more trust than a perfect score. Sort by Newest, read the low ratings and walk away from any salon that offers you something in return for a review. Every salon's figures, with their date, appear in our ranking of Da Nang nail salons.

faq.q: Are Google reviews of Da Nang nail salons reliable?
faq.r: Mostly, for salons with a long and steady review history. Read the newest reviews and the low ratings before trusting a 5.0, and be wary of sudden bursts.

faq.q: Is a salon allowed to give a discount for a Google review?
faq.r: Google's review policy does not allow offering anything in exchange for a review, including discounts or free add-ons. A salon can ask every customer for an honest review, with no reward and without asking only the happy ones.

faq.q: What should I do if I think a review is fake?
faq.r: Use Report review on Google Maps for that review. Then judge the salon in person with the 90-second check: single-use tools, a working steriliser, prices in writing.
